summary: Windows restores submitted name failures by local actor, board and item without replay. Workbench removes the matching failure before running the conditional save and records a new failure only on rejection. Unreadable recovery leaves the accepted board visible and its local file untouched.
evidence: Final focused run: cargo test --locked -p boardcraft-desktop --features native-smoke --test windows_smoke failed_name_reopens_only_for_actor_and_board -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture passed (1 passed, 3 filtered). Fresh Windows Kit processes shared an isolated recovery directory. Fresh PostgreSQL connections checked both ordered IDs, titles and revisions at each checkpoint.

The second Review rejected three spaces. The same actor and board reopened with both accepted labels, the exact failed request, validation reason, Retry change and Dismiss, with no editor or submission. Dismiss survived another launch; IDs 42 then 17 both stayed Review/1. For the fixture-faulted padded request, another actor on the same board and the original actor on a different board with identical item IDs each saw clean rows and zero submissions.

After removing the fixture fault, the original scope restored the database failure with no replay. Explicit Retry projected exactly ' Coral ' once. PostgreSQL confirmed the retry was waiting on the fixture lock. Before releasing it, a fresh same-scope window showed both Review labels, no editor or failure actions and zero submissions; an independent read still saw both rows at revision 1. After release, only ID 17 became Coral/2. A further launch showed the committed labels and no failure.

With malformed recovery bytes, the fresh window showed a visible unreadable-recovery warning above both accepted rows. A subsequent blank edit was rejected in that window. The file matched its original corrupt bytes at both checkpoints and neither stored row changed.

Coordinator reference comparison: the isolated board screen, real name cell, queue and storage ran against a disposable save-operation fixture. The reference keys its queue and failure snapshot by actor and board, not view. A fresh parent in the same session and a fresh session reading persistent storage both restored the failure with no detail or save call. Changing either identity restored nothing. The failed spaces survived until Dismiss; reopening after Dismiss left both rows at Review/1. Retry of the transient failure made one detail read and one padded name-only save, clearing recovery before commit and advancing only the second row to Coral/2. This compared client scoping, not signed-in access or end-to-end HTTP.

The reference keeps a tab-local snapshot with persistent fallback. Dismissing an older snapshot kept that tab clean but preserved a newer persistent copy for a fresh session. Malformed bytes warned without hiding the grid; explicit discard cleared them with zero saves. Windows guards cleanup by failure occurrence and preserves unreadable data. Independent-window refresh, in-app unreadable-data repair and signed-in actor selection remain open. Unsubmitted cell drafts have a separate reference lifetime and are not covered by this failed-request store.

After review, node scripts/run.mjs run 1 verified 11-windows-failure-reopen: formatting, all 14 runner regressions, both local recovery tests, the desktop_edit database case and all four named graphical Windows cases passed. git diff --check passed. Prior gates remained intact; this Windows-only packet did not rerun Android.
